column3: The Hebrew separately narrates His rescuing them; BSB makes protection a purpose. The Hebrew has enemy and one lying in ambush in the singular; BSB has enemies and bandits in the plural.
The Hebrew says they stayed there; BSB says they rested there.
The Hebrew uses the passive “was weighed”; BSB says “we weighed out.” It says articles without explicitly repeating “sacred,” which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew says “by number, by weight, for everything” without a separate verification verb; BSB explicitly says everything was verified.
The Hebrew calls them sons of the exile; BSB says exiles.
The Hebrew names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
